pr_title: EQL: Remove unused classes from reponse API
pr_body:
Remove Count class and related artifacts since that functionality is not
(yet) available.
Update parser name for better error reporting.

Fix #62131
pr_comments: I'll open up a separate PR for this for master (8.0.0). The upgrade path there means latest 7.x which means the backwards check is not needed.

issue_context.title: EQL: Clean the java client API / internal response
issue_context.body:
Currently the Java API as well as the internal response has the structure for future response (such as `Count`) despite this not being actually implemented or on the near future roadmap.
As such the code should be removed - there's nothing preventing us from adding it later but having it there without any usage is just useless.

review_comments: The name here looks like a mistake (left-over from count I presume) so I've changed it to hits instead to preserve the current naming conventions.
This will break requests in mixed clusters, are we ok with that?

Thanks for flagging this.
EQL is currently experimental so the BWC compatibility is loose however I'd like where possible, to avoid this situation. I've added this topic to the agenda since I can see other areas where this *might* affect us (like using fields API) and we could use more testing.

Yeah, I am not sure that experimental necessarily means we don't support rolling restarts. My interpretation was that we can break it if there is a compelling reason for it. So, I would lean towards supporting it whenever possible. Two things we need to keep in mind: 1) if we will ever promote it to non-experimental in some 7.x release this might break rolling upgrade in 7.x. and 2) if we will promote it sometime in 8.x, we should be careful about breaking BWC with 7.last.

I've added a compatibility branch just to be safe. We never created `Counter` there's no actual instance to be read, just the bool which should be `false` always.
Nevertheless I've added the previous code since it was small.
This file is just added in with small clean-up (removal of unused variables).
